clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A client with an external fixator is preparing for discharge. Which statement shows correct understanding of pin-site care?

options.A: I will follow the pin-site care plan given by my orthopedic team and report new drainage, increasing redness, or loosening of a pin or frame component.
options.B: I can choose any routine online cleansing schedule because every external-fixator pin site requires the same care regimen.
options.C: I do not need to assess the pin sites after discharge because infection risk ends after the pins are inserted.
options.D: I can ignore increasing redness or drainage unless the entire external-fixator frame becomes unstable.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current NCBI StatPearls guidance states that pin-site care is important but techniques vary considerably and evidence has not established one universal protocol as superior for all external fixators. It identifies drainage or erythema around pins as findings that require pin-site attention and lists pin-site infection, osteomyelitis, and frame or pin/wire failure or loosening among recognized complications. Nursing and orthopedic teams should assess pin sites, soft-tissue integrity, and neurovascular status and report problems to the treating clinician. Therefore the client should follow the individualized orthopedic plan rather than substitute a universal self-selected regimen and should report concerning pin-site or hardware changes.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach clients with external fixation to follow their prescribed pin-site care protocol and promptly report drainage, increasing erythema, or hardware loosening rather than assuming a universal cleansing regimen.
semantic_correction.source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), StatPearls
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Last updated August 4, 2023; StatPearls 2026 edition accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: Pin Site Care — care techniques vary considerably and no universal superior protocol is established; drainage or erythema around pins requires pin-site attention. semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: External-fixator pin-site care is not governed by one universally superior cleansing protocol; drainage/erythema and hardware loosening are clinically relevant changes requiring assessment and communication with the treating team.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed 'all/only' distractor cueing, shortened the correct answer, and limited the item to source-supported individualized pin-site care plus drainage/erythema and hardware-loosening reporting.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item avoids inventing one universal cleaning solution or frequency and tests clinically supported monitoring and communication.

option_audit.A: Correct. It reflects individualized pin-site care and reporting of source-supported infection/hardware warning findings.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Evidence does not establish one universal pin-care protocol for every external fixator.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Pin-site infection and other complications remain possible while the device is in place and require ongoing monitoring.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Increasing erythema or drainage warrants assessment before the entire frame becomes unstable.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone preserves individualized care while identifying source-supported changes that require clinical attention.
cueing_check: All four choices are pin-site care statements of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
